about.title: Hesperia Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Hesperia sits along I-15 where High Desert commuters, long-haul trucks, and weekend travelers share the same lanes. In 2025, the city logged 442 injury collisions, with 702 people hurt and 11 lives lost. Main Street, Bear Valley Road, and Mariposa Road appear most often in those public reports, and the counts tend to climb on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the practical steps matter right away: photograph the scene and the vehicles, keep every medical record, and decline to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement until you have spoken with a lawyer. California gives most people two years to file, but claims involving a public agency can require a notice in as little as six months. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Hesperia residents with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case recovers something.

whyChoose.title: Why Hesperia Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines in the High Desert are shorter than they look
items.desc: Two years sounds like plenty of time, yet a claim tied to a city or county vehicle, or a road maintained by Caltrans, may need a formal claim within six months. An attorney can flag that early.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly to blame for a collision on Bear Valley Road, you can still pursue the portion of your losses the other driver caused.

items.title: Nothing out of pocket to get started
items.desc: Our connection service is free, and the independent attorneys in the network handle car accident cases on contingency. If there is no recovery, you owe no attorney fee.

items.question: The other driver's insurer keeps calling for a recorded statement. Do I have to give one?
items.answer: No. You have no obligation to give a recorded statement to another driver's insurance company, and doing so before you understand your injuries can hurt your claim. Politely decline, jot down who called and when, and let an attorney handle those conversations.

items.question: My crash happened on I-15 near the Main Street exit. Does the freeway location change anything?
items.answer: It can. Freeway collisions in Hesperia are typically handled by the CHP rather than city police, so the report comes from a different agency, and if road conditions or state equipment played a part, a government entity may be involved. That can shorten the filing window to as little as six months, which makes an early review worthwhile.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can claim for pain and suffering in California?
items.answer: For an ordinary car accident, California does not cap non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. What you can recover depends on the evidence, the extent of your injuries, and how fault is divided. No attorney can promise a particular result, but preserving records and photos helps present the full picture.
